name: Meridian Munitions Street PDW MSP-7 'Alleycat'
description:
The MSP-7 Alleycat is Meridian Munitions' dedicated street-level PDW, designed for the reality of urban self-defense in Tier 2-3 zones. The weapon fires 5.7mm caseless from a 20-round magazine and features Meridian's open-architecture BCI module for operators who have basic neural interfaces. For those without BCI, the weapon includes conventional micro red-dot sights and a manual safety.

The Alleycat's distinguishing feature is its integrated smart-holster system. The weapon's grip contains a biometric lock that releases only for registered users, preventing the weapon from being used against its owner if seized. The holster communicates with the weapon's BCI module to track draw/reholster cycles, and Meridian's companion app provides usage analytics that many operators find useful for training.

At Φ1,800, the Alleycat sits comfortably in the affordable professional range. It is not cheap enough to be disposable or expensive enough to represent an investment. It is a working tool priced for working people — exactly the market Meridian has cultivated. The weapon is reliable without being remarkable, accurate without being precise, and effective without being devastating.
specifications:
caliber: 5.7mm caseless
effective_range: 100m
rate_of_fire: 800 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 20 rounds
weight: 1.4 kg
tactical_use: The Alleycat provides reliable personal defense for urban operators. Its biometric grip lock ensures the weapon cannot be turned against its owner, and the dual BCI/manual operation means it functions regardless of the operator's augmentation level. The 5.7mm round offers better penetration than 9mm against soft armor while remaining controllable in the lightweight platform. The smart-holster analytics help operators train their draw speed and weapon handling.
cultural_context: The Alleycat is the PDW of GLMZ's urban middle class — security contractors, shop owners in rough neighborhoods, and anyone whose daily commute passes through contested zones. It is the weapon equivalent of a reliable car: not exciting, not prestigious, but always there when you need it. Meridian's marketing emphasizes the Alleycat's approachability, featuring ordinary people in ordinary situations rather than operators in tactical gear.
story_hooks: An Alleycat's biometric lock was hacked, and the weapon was used in a crime while still registered to its original owner. The forensic trail leads back to the victim, not the perpetrator.
Meridian's companion app usage data was subpoenaed by a corponation, revealing the locations and weapon-handling habits of thousands of Alleycat owners — a privacy nightmare.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular PDW with a distinctly modern aesthetic—sharp edges and aggressive lines suggest street-ready pragmatism over military grandeur. The profile is lean and purposeful, designed to sit flat against the body when holstered. The overall impression is 'efficient tool' rather than 'statement weapon.'
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 38cm (stock collapsed); Barrel: 12cm; Width at grip: 4.2cm; Height: 18cm (including mounted sight)
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and responsive—1.4kg feels almost negligible when held, allowing for quick target acquisition and minimal fatigue during extended carry. The weight distribution favors the grip, creating natural pivot points for street-precision shooting.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel barrel assembly and internal action; grip module is machined aluminum for biometric sensor integration
physical_description.finish: Matte polymer body with a slight texture to reduce glare; steel components feature a dark gunmetal DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating that resists corrosion in urban environments
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray polymer with gunmetal accents; BCI module connector highlighted in muted cyan (Meridian's corporate accent color); slight oxidized patina on steel visible under angled light
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with micro-ridged patterns for wet conditions; the biometric sensor zone feels slightly raised and smoother than the surrounding grip—deliberately distinct so the operator's thumb naturally seats on the unlock point
distinctive_features: Integrated biometric sensor strip running vertically down the grip (faintly illuminates amber when unpowered, cyan when active)
Dual-mode sight rail with both micro red-dot mount and manual iron sight backup
Oversized charging handle with textured grooves for gloved operation
Smart-holster communication port (recessed USB-C equivalent marked with Φ symbol)
Ambidextrous mag release with aggressive ribs
Vented slide top to manage heat signature
Serialized manufacturer plate recessed into left side of frame
Wear pattern near trigger guard suggesting field use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Meridian Munitions logo stamped into left receiver—stylized 'M' with meridian line through center; 'MSP-7 ALLEYCAT' printed in small caps on right side of barrel shroud; manufacturing date code laser-etched above mag well; serial number on raised plate below rear sight
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but not pristine—this is a working tool. Light scuffing on polymer, minor salt corrosion on exposed steel, grip shows subtle wear at the biometric sensor point from thousands of registered touches. No battle damage, but evidence of professional daily carry.
